fix(launch): strip repository-scoped variables once at scope build

The launcher's scope now holds its owner's environment less the
repository-scoped variables, so every child inherits that copy and an
overlay applies over it as given; the lifeline spawns with it too. The
renderer's boot hands on the same stripped environment. The list is
renamed for what it holds, its git part marked as a copy of git's, and
stale doctor citations and comments are corrected. The daemon case
moves into the existing PR-state fixture.

fix(launch): withhold repository-naming variables from the inherited base only

An overlay is a launch's explicit intent, so a variable it names now
reaches the child as given; only the ambient inherited environment loses
the names. The never-keyed overlay type and its type-level test go.

fix(launch): type the overlay against repository-naming variables and derive the forge part from the table

Each forge entry carries its CLI and the variable it reads as its
repository, and the withheld list derives its forge part from the
table, so a new forge cannot leave its variable out. An overlay naming
one of those variables no longer type-checks. The memory note says the
daemon's own environment still carries them.

fix(launch): withhold repository-local variables from inherited child environments

A daemon spawned from a git hook, a rebase --exec or a vcsh shell
inherits GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE and GH_REPO, which git and gh honour
ahead of the working directory. The launcher's one environment builder
now withholds git's repository-local set plus GH_REPO and GITLAB_REPO
from every child that inherits the owner's environment, after any
overlay. A session's own environment passes unchanged. The forge table
moves to a leaf module beside the list; plugin install no longer asks
git for the list at runtime.

Merge 289d3535bbea47cb30c6a511ab2c4f0bf1ad1cc3 into 4521bf6f3ff8442f1ade1eb3785e9b245dd454e6
fix(config): every state variable reads its key through one fold

fix(config): every reader of a placement setting reads its one fold

A placement setting's draft slot keeps its fold in the store, so the bar,
the slot's control, a picker's mark and a carousel all show the value the
placement draws. A click, which reads no store, folds the session's key
through the same function.

The resolution and a placement carry a stale pick as data, the setting and
the spelling stored. The draw writes the sentence where the worn name is
known, so a rule-decided theme is named and a placement following the bar
names the bar's theme. A retired theme names the theme to write. A
placement setting is reported only when its draw reads it, and once per
slot when its label is drawn beside it.

A save keeps a stale pick stored. The edit-mode stepper steps from the
value it shows, the staged one included. A plain state key's stored value
is read against its range, so an out-of-range value steps from the default
instead of failing the click.

The loader checks theme names against the installed themes alone, the
authority the gate and the render use.

fix(config): a stale session pick draws the fallback under a warning

A session's stored setting can name something outside its domain: a theme
this build doesn't install, a style or preset the config no longer
declares, a dropped effect or endcaps shape, an out-of-range padding, a
placement theme naming nothing installed. Each used to draw the fallback
silently, and the stepper clamped an out-of-range int the render refused,
so a `+` click could move the bar the wrong way.

Each setting now reads its stored spelling through its own parse into one
shape (unset, held, or stale carrying the spelling), and the one fold
reports what it passed over only where the session's rung would have been
in force. The draw shows one `stale` warning per key, naming the setting,
the stored value and what the bar wears. The stored value stays, so a
config that declares the member again brings the pick back. Steppers step
from the folded value the bar shows. Installed-theme membership has one
authority, shared by the write gate, the theme read and placements.
